A tiny fish bone, a major surgical challenge, and a valuable lesson in timely diagnosis.

I recently had the opportunity to  manage  a rare and complex case involving an 11-year-old girl who presented with persistent throat pain and difficulty swallowing after a fish meal.

What initially appeared to be a routine fish bone impaction turned out to be far more serious. Advanced imaging revealed that the fish bone had perforated the food pipe and migrated into the thyroid gland, leading to a deep neck infection and abscess formation.

The case required careful planning and open neck surgery to safely remove the foreign body while preserving critical structures responsible for voice function and calcium regulation.

I am pleased that the patient made an excellent recovery and has returned to her normal activities.

 Persistent symptoms should never be dismissed.

Extremely unprofessional and disrespectful clinic.
We had a confirmed 7:15 PM appointment with Dr. Bhavik and reached at 7:00 PM. There was barely any crowd. We could clearly hear the doctor consulting one patient and assumed we were next.

Instead, the receptionist asked us to wait in another room.
We waited until 7:50 PM without a single update. When we followed up, the receptionist casually said it would take more time — no explanation, no apology, nothing. We continued waiting until 8:00 PM, only to then be informed that Dr. Bhavik had already left and another doctor would see us. This was never communicated beforehand.
How does a doctor leave when patients with appointments are still waiting?
Even after agreeing to consult the other doctor, we were made to wait again — despite there being no visible patients. Repeated requests to send us in were ignored. The staff and the other doctor seemed completely indifferent to patients’ time.
This clinic clearly does not respect appointments or basic professionalism. If you value your time, avoid this place. They do not even deserve this one star..

Update after the clinic response:

The response shared by the clinic does not reflect the actual experience.
We were informed about Dr. Bhavik leaving only around 8:00 PM, well after we had already been waiting. Even after agreeing to consult the associate doctor, we were still made to wait while the doctor appeared to have no patients at that time.
What was most disappointing was the lack of clear communication from the receptionist despite us asking multiple times. We did not leave immediately as suggested in the response — we waited and only left after repeatedly asking and receiving no proper update or effort to arrange the consultation.
Medical emergencies can happen, and that is understandable. However, basic transparency and respect for patients’ time should still be maintained. Unfortunately, that was not the case during our visit, and the response here seems more like a justification than an accurate representation of what happened.
